topic: Tesla starts rolling out FSD (Supervised) v15, whose driving AI now draws what it plans to do (Reality View)
announced_at: 21 November 2026 (Tesla's X post, 19:24 UTC; coverage 21-22 Nov)
why_selected: Strongest eligible story after the V7 verification gate: a visual, widely discussed product change with a clear consequence (can you see what the car will do?).
why_short: Tesla's FSD now draws its own plan on screen.
why_beats_alternatives: OpenRouter's prompt-theft story scored higher (69.5) but is a security-breach claim whose notice and study could not be opened, so it fails the V7 extraordinary-claims rule; Amazon's AI-agent zero-day story (63.0) was published on 20 Nov, before the window; FBI NCIC, Waymo recalls and the Decart deal are older, unconfirmed or an unsigned billion-dollar report. Tesla's rollout is confirmed by Tesla's own post and independent coverage inside the window, and it is easy to show.
why_this_story: Tesla began rolling out FSD (Supervised) v15 on 21 Nov, and its headline feature, Reality View, draws the car's planned turns on screen: a rare look at what a driving AI intends. It is visual, easy to grasp and invites a trust debate. X signal: Tesla's and its AI lead's posts were seen only in search results; engagement is unverified (x.com blocked). It beat OpenRouter's prompt-theft story, which failed the extraordinary-claims check, and older or unconfirmed stories (Amazon zero-day, FBI breach, Decart deal).
verified_development: On 21 Nov 2026 Tesla posted that FSD v15 is starting to roll out (update 2026.38.6.11, FSD Supervised v15.0.1, first wave). Its head of AI software says the driving model now also renders Reality View, a live view whose arrows show planned turns. Tesla claims a 25x better critical intervention rate without published numbers.
disclosure: Disclosure: written by Claude, an Anthropic model. Tesla and xAI are not Anthropic; no conflict known.
research_summary: A fresh research pass covered 23 developments from 21-22 Nov across AI labs, tools, creator tech, robotics, cybersecurity, fintech and policy. Ten were eligible inside the 24-hour window. The highest scorer, OpenRouter removing three inference providers after a Dragos study of prompt theft, was held under the V7 extraordinary-claims rule because neither the notice nor the study could be opened. Tesla's FSD (Supervised) v15 rollout is the next eligible story: Tesla's own post and its head of AI software announced it on 21 Nov, and Tesla North, paultan.org, Electrek and techAU covered it. Reality View is the visual hook; the 25x claim is Tesla's, with no published baseline. All social metrics are unknown because x.com cannot be opened here.

primary_sources.label: Tesla on X: FSD v15 now starting to roll out (21 Nov 2026)
Ashok Elluswamy on X: Reality View (21 Nov 2026)

key_facts: Reality View: the driving model renders a live view; arrows show planned turns (Tesla's description).
25x critical intervention claim is Tesla's own, no published baseline.
uncertainties: How many cars received v15 and in which countries (first wave reported in the US).
Hardware coverage: reports say HW4/AI4 first; whether HW3 cars get it is unclear.
Tesla has not defined or published the data behind the 25x claim; no independent test exists.
A realistic rendering is not proof the car understands the scene perfectly.
Tesla's posts and every news page were read through search results; none could be opened (DNS blocked).
excluded_claims: Hardware details (HW3 vs HW4) where reports differ.
Speed Camera Slowdown, Bike Rack Mode and other release-note items (not central).
context: FSD (Supervised) still requires an attentive driver. Earlier versions showed a simpler, game-like visualization; Reality View replaces it with a rendered scene from the driving model itself.
script:
Tesla's driving AI now shows you what it's about to do.

On November 21, Tesla started rolling out FSD Supervised version 15 to a first wave of owners.

The new feature is called Reality View.

Tesla's head of AI software says the model that drives the car also draws the road around it, live.

Arrows show the turns it plans to take.

Tesla claims a 25x improvement in critical interventions. That's Tesla's own number, not an independent test.

Would seeing its plan make you trust it more?

audience_check.why_care_today: It started rolling out yesterday and the clips are spreading.

hook_clarity.why: First line says exactly what is new in eleven plain words.

factual_accuracy.why: Every sentence maps to claims c1-c4 with attributions spoken aloud.

natural_delivery.why: Short spoken sentences; read aloud twice at a normal pace.

narrative_coherence.why: One idea throughout: the car shows its plan, and can you trust it.

audience_relevance.why: Self-driving trust is a broad, current debate beyond Tesla owners.

practical_takeaway.why: Says who has it now and flags the unverified 25x claim before viewers repeat it.

ending_quality.why: Ends on a natural trust question that invites comments.

no_redundancy.why: No sentence repeats the headline or another sentence.

no_jargon.why: Only 'critical interventions' is technical, and it reads plainly in context.

no_unsupported_implications.why: Never says the car is self-driving or safer; the 25x claim is labelled Tesla's own.

recording_guidance.final_tone: Curious and even-handed, not a fan and not a critic.
